transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Nova Finance - Eng Mgr), Ethan Walker (Nova - Platform), Maya Patel (Nova - Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/sdk-quickstart (sample repo), https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (security deck)

Summary: quick SDK integration walkthrough (Python + TypeScript), auth patterns (api key vs sso/saml), environment setup, demos of Redwood Console and Optimize suggestions, next steps: send quickstart repo, SOC2 docs, schedule POC kickoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Avery, AE for Nova Finance. with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya (Nova): Hi, doing well, thanks. excited to see the SDK flow, we want to get a basic integration by end of month.
[00:12] Diego (Redwood SE): great. agenda: quick auth + env setup, python and ts quickstarts, show console for keys and monitoring, then a brief on Optimize recommendations for cost & latency. we'll leave time for Qs.
[00:20] Ethan (Nova): Sounds good — primary constraints: sub-100ms p50 for short queries, and token cost is a big factor. also security team will want encryption/KMS details.
[00:30] Maya (Nova-Sec): yes SOC2, SSO/SAML and audit logs are must-haves.
[00:35] Avery: good callouts. we'll cover auth and the security docs we'll share after. starting with auth — two common flows: API key for dev / server-to-server, and SSO (SAML/OIDC) for corporate console access. for production we recommend customer-managed KMS when using Private, or our key wrapping via KMS for hosted.
[00:50] Priya: timeline question — can we use hosted API initially then move to dedicated if needed?
[00:55] Diego: absolutely. Redwood API is the fastest path: simple REST/SDK, same endpoints across hosted/dedicated/private. you can pin model versions in config and route. test on hosted, then we can provision dedicated capacity with predictable throughput for the POC.
[01:10] Avery: I'll note that as a next step — provision trial dedicated capacity if you want.
[01:15] Diego: jumping into code — Python quickstart first. (link pasted) the pattern is very small: pip install redwood-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env, then client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) and call client.text.generate(...). this is demo code, but your engineers will have a runnable sample in the repo.
[01:32] [screen share sound] Diego: I'll paste a snippet for TypeScript too — npm install @redwood/sdk, set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY, and use const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
[01:50] Priya: Any opinion on storing keys? we use vault for secrets.
[01:55] Diego: Perfect — we recommend storing API keys in Vault or your cloud secret manager. for server-side calls use short-lived keys if possible. for client-side or browser, route through your backend to avoid exposing keys.
[02:08] Maya: For SSO to the console, do you support SAML?
[02:12] Avery: Yes we support SAML and OIDC. we'll share the SSO setup doc. console access can be scoped with RBAC and org/team roles. audit logs are available and we can route logs to your SIEM.
[02:25] Ethan: want to confirm: can we restrict model access per team?
[02:28] Diego: yes, per-route and per-model permissions in the Console. you can also set quotas.
[02:33] Priya: Great. show us a sample env setup for a dev machine and for CI.
[02:38] Diego: Dev: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx; start local quickstart which calls Redwood. CI: store key in your CI secrets, run integration tests with a small token budget, we recommend using a test model or lower-capacity variant to save cost.
[02:52] [pause, typing]
[02:58] Diego: Quick demo of Console — here is the API keys page, create key, revoke, view usage. on the models page you can see curated open weights we surface and perf notes like p50 latency and per-token cost estimates.
[03:15] Priya: Does Console expose Optimize suggestions?
[03:18] Diego: Yeah — Optimize gives recommendations: batching window suggestions, quantization hints, cacheable prefixes, and model swaps for cheaper variants. it ties recommendations to traffic patterns you can simulate in the console.
[03:32] Maya: For security, where do you store logs and how long are they retained?
[03:36] Avery: by default we retain logs for 30 days in hosted. for enterprise we offer longer retention and the option to forward logs to your S3 / SIEM. audit logs are part of the enterprise package.
[03:50] Priya: around latency: you mentioned kv cache earlier in the docs — how does that help short queries?
[03:55] Diego: KV cache stores key/value attention caches for repeating prefixes, so for chat-like flows you can avoid re-computing earlier tokens. it's especially helpful for assistant-style workloads — reduces per-token compute and latency. sometimes the transcription on our docs says K-V cash, sorry that's a bad auto transcription.
[04:08] Ethan: metrics — what's exposed for per-token cost and p50/p95?
[04:12] Diego: Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency (p50/p90/p95), and you can trace tokens back to requests. also exportable CSV for billing alignment.
[04:24] Priya: okay, looking at quickstarts — we want both python and ts sample apps.
[04:28] Diego: repo includes both: python/quickstart.py and ts/examples/chat.ts. we'll include a sample docker-compose for an integration test.
[04:38] Avery: for the POC success criteria, Priya mentioned sub-100ms p50 and cost target. can you share throughput numbers?
[04:45] Priya: target is 200 reqs/sec with avg message 50 tokens. cost threshold is important — ideally under $0.005 per request but flexible.
[04:55] Diego: we'll run a baseline on hosted, then we can provision a dedicated pool and run the same workload. dedicated will give you predictable throughput and can hit tighter p50s depending on model and batching.
[05:08] [interruptions / cross talk]
[05:15] Maya: encryption — do you support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[05:18] Avery: for hosted we have KMS integrations and envelope encryption; for Private or on-prem you can use your own KMS/HSM, yes. we'll share the exact security spec in the doc.
[05:30] Diego: quick note about function/tool calling and streaming — our SDK supports streaming responses and function calling patterns; streaming helps perceived latency for long responses.
[05:43] Ethan: any gotchas migrating from hosted to dedicated?
[05:46] Diego: models are compatible; we handle model variants and routing. main differences are capacity planning: dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and autoscale/burst options. config is similar, but we'll help you pin model versions and test fallbacks.
[05:58] Priya: ok can you run a short demo — python quickstart live?
[06:02] Diego: sure — running the sample now — (typing) — "python quickstart.py" — it hits the client, returns a short completion in 220ms on my local to hosted endpoint. note dev net is variable, but you can see how the SDK logs request/response and tokens.
[06:23] [96% packet loss joke? laughter]
[06:30] Priya: nice. can you show typescript sample?
[06:33] Diego: (switching) ts sample: node chat.js — returns in about 240ms. both samples are intentionally simple. repo includes unit test that mocks responses.
[06:45] Avery: next steps recap: we'll send the SDK quickstart repo, SOC2 deck, and a proposed POC plan with dedicated trial. Diego will run a latency baseline and share results. Priya to send prompt sets and traffic profile.
[06:58] Priya: we'll get prompt sets and verify timeline.
[07:04] Ethan: security will review SOC2 and SSO flow.
[07:08] Maya: yes we'll add a compliance reviewer to the thread.
[07:12] Avery: perfect. any other questions?
[07:15] Priya: one more — how do rollouts work if we want to A/B test two model variants?
[07:19] Diego: Console supports canary and A/B rollouts by traffic percentage per route; automatic fallback policies if a model fails or latency spikes.
[07:28] Priya: great.
[07:30] Avery: thanks everyone — I'll follow up with links and a proposed POC kickoff for 2026-03-30.
[07:36] Priya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
